thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV-1 - Multiple GPU serving hosts reporting NCCL hangs and container restarts in tp/pp jobs. Affected cluster: gpu-prod-us-west-2. Pager epoch: 1800123456 :rotating_light:

devon_sre: acknowledging pager, I'm on it. starting timeline + triage.

maria_oncall: saw alerts ~ 1800123440, job ids: run-2278, run-2281. customers hitting 502s and sustained tail latency spikes.

alex_runtime: quick summary from logs: repeated `NCCL ERROR 4` (unhandled timeout) then `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in communicator init, then container killed by OOM. stack shows stall in allreduce across tp shards.

devon_sre: pasting sanitized excerpt:```
[2026-11-02 18:24:12] NCCL INFO commId 0x7f9b... timeout detected
[2026-11-02 18:24:12] NCCL ERROR 4 -> TIMEOUT (rank 0 -> rank 3)
[2026-11-02 18:24:13] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-11-02 18:24:15] Container runtime: process exited with code 137
```

jamal_prodeng: customers impacted: two sandbox customers and a midmarket embedder job. Support ticket list updated (TKT-5941, TKT-5942). marking potential data-safe (no PII leaked).

irene_support: adding customer-facing note: "We are investigating a multi-GPU runtime issue causing intermittent failures and increased latency. No data loss expected."

alex_runtime: initial hypothesis: combination of NCCL timeout (network hiccup / IB flap) plus aggressive KV cache growth in PP causing OOM during communicator reset. Also seeing netlink: `mlx5: port X link down` on host gpu-07.

devon_sre: running quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-07` returns multiple restartCount > 3. `ssh gpu-07` -> `dmesg` shows `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79: process killed` and `mlx5` port flaps.

maria_oncall: immediate mitigation suggestions?

alex_runtime: recommend 1) cordon + drain gpu-07, 2) restart node's RDMA stack / `systemctl restart rdma` (if available), 3) restart container runtime on node (containerd/cri), 4) force communicator re-init for inflight jobs by killing worker processes gracefully.

devon_sre: executing drain: `kubectl cordon gpu-07 && kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — started. moving traffic off.

deploy-bot: Deploy job queued: scale up fallback pool `inference-fallback-gpu` +2 replicas (requested by devon_sre).

jamal_prodeng: while draining, can we flip a routing rule to route new TP/PP requests to single-GPU fallback model? We have a fallback policy in Console -> Rollouts.

alex_runtime: yes—initiate temporary config: `route-model: tp_v2 -> tp_v2-single-gpu` for requests with route tag `prod_tp`. This will reduce throughput but keep latency steady. Doing the switch now.

incident-bot: Action logged: routing override applied by alex_runtime at 1800123523.

irene_support: notifying customers impacted that we're routing to fallback to reduce failures; might see reduced throughput.

devon_sre: drain completed. node gpu-07 now in `SchedulingDisabled`. attempted `systemctl restart rdma` -> success. `ip link show` shows port restored. restarting containerd to clear zombie processes.

alex_runtime: after these steps, new jobs on other nodes still saw a few NCCL timeouts; suspect communicator state corruption persisted for jobs that were mid-allreduce. For running jobs, we've been issuing graceful restarts: `pkill -INT -f model_worker` which triggers checkpoint+resume logic.

maria_oncall: customer impact update: error rates down from 12% -> 2% over 12 minutes since rollout of fallback. Critical customers A and B now stable on fallback.

jamal_prodeng: ok good. any immediate root cause?

alex_runtime: collecting artifacts: NCCL logs, `nvidia-smi topo -m`, kernel dmesg, rdma counters. One oddity: mixed NCCL versions on nodes (v2.14 on gpu-07, v2.12 elsewhere) — could cause communicator handshake issues when rolling upgrades occurred last week. Also saw `nv_peer_mem` messages about peer registration failing after reboot.

devon_sre: saving logs to GCS: `gs://redwood-incidents/1800123456/nccl-logs.tar.gz`. started a live capture of `nvidia-smi dmon` and `tcpdump` on the host for 30m.

alex_runtime: temporary hardening steps: set env `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^docker0` for the runtime, bump `NCCL_TIMEOUT=600` to allow slow allreduce during degraded network. These are applied cluster-wide as emergency overrides.

devon_sre: applied overrides at 1800123568, config rollout in progress (daemonset restart).

deploy-bot: cluster config rollout completed on 5/6 nodes; gpu-07 excluded.

maria_oncall: have we restarted affected customer jobs yet or letting them auto-requeue?

alex_runtime: for low-importance jobs, let auto-requeue. For the two midmarket jobs we manually triggered job restart after clearing node state — they came back clean.

jamal_prodeng: next steps for long-term: 1) reconcile NCCL versions across fleet, 2) audit recent kernel/firmware patches that touched mlx5 drivers, 3) add guardrail to detect mixed-NCCL handshake and fail fast to avoid OOM cascades.

irene_support: preparing a short customer summary for the affected tenants to go out in ~30m.

devon_sre: handing off to eng-runtime for root cause and durable fix. primary assignee: alex_runtime (lead), secondary: devon_sre (sre). Please continue the thread and tag me for postmortem.

alex_runtime: taking ownership. immediate ticket: RINF-3172. I'll run full fleet audit for NCCL package version and schedule coordinated upgrade with rolling reboots on low-traffic windows. dropping notes to runbook: /runbooks/collective-failure.md — adding checklist to ensure `nv_peer_mem` and `mlx5` firmware compatibility.

devon_sre: postmortem timeline: will start draft within 24h; include mitigation timeline, customer impact, and follow-ups (NCCL pin, RDMA health checks, route fallback automation). tagging eng-sre and eng-platform.

maria_oncall: thanks team. marking pager resolved at 1800123670 — service restored to acceptable error rates, fallback routing still active until we confirm fleet stability.

incident-bot: Pager closed by maria_oncall at 1800123670.

jamal_prodeng: note for postmortem: estimate cost delta from fallback and extra instances. I'll add numbers to the incident doc.

alex_runtime: will run a test matrix in staging to reproduce with artificial RDMA drops and mixed NCCL versions. If we can repro, we'll validate an automatic rollback to single-GPU fallback for affected shards.

devon_sre: leaving this thread open for follow-ups. please update RINF-3172 with any new findings and tag #oncall when you need another paging cycle.

irene_support: posted initial customer note; will post update once we have a root cause.

maria_oncall: handoff complete. switching to monitoring watch.

(End of thread)
